meta.title: Starbucks, Priced for the Comeback
meta.dek: Brian Niccol has brought the customers back. The stock got paid for that on the day he was hired. What does $98 assume about the part that hasn’t come back yet, the margin?
meta.type: Global specialty-coffee retail, shifting from company-operated toward licensed

verdict.sentence: The traffic turnaround is real, but at 38× earnings the price already assumes near-Bull margins; the probability-weighted case pays [[pw_return]] a year against the 13% hurdle.
verdict.breaks_if: Q4 non-GAAP operating margin falls back below ~12% once the one-time tariff refund is gone, putting the FY2028 target of 13.5–15% out of reach.

call: Niccol has done the hard part: US transactions have grown three quarters running (+3.0%, +4.3%, +4.2%), with ticket rising alongside traffic. The price banked it on August 13, 2024 and then some. At $98 no Bear probability earns even an ordinary 9% a year; the price needs FY2031 non-GAAP EPS of about [[Priced-in.eps]], close to our Bull. We give the Bear 25% because the margin walk is weaker than the headline: Q3's 14.4% carried ~80 bps of one-time tariff refunds, North America is still ~9 points below FY2023, and two-year traffic is only +0.3%. Five years of dividends and buybacks exceeded net income, so nothing is retained to fund the 8,000 uplifts, and the FT's report of a Chipotle bid exploration (denied) is a capital-allocation flag. Good business; the PW case returns [[pw_return]] and clears 13% only at [[entry]].

tests.claim: That the margin walk holds without the refund.
tests.test: in Q4 FY2026 (Oct 29), non-GAAP operating margin ≥13% for the quarter, the >11% full-year guide delivered, and an FY2027 guide that keeps 13.5–15% in FY2028 in reach.
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Bull to Bear (PW EV [[test1.pw_ev]], [[test1.pw_return]]/yr) → stays **[[test1.verb]]**, entry falls to [[test1.entry]].

tests.claim: That traffic survives the toughest compare.
tests.test: Q4 US comp at or above the 6.5% guide with transactions positive, then Q1 FY2027 (late January) positive against Q1's +3%.
tests.if_fail: Base FY2031 EPS cut to ≈$4.20, margin-only growth (PW EV [[test2.pw_ev]], [[test2.pw_return]]/yr) → stays **[[test2.verb]]**, entry [[test2.entry]].

tests.claim: That owner earnings cover the dividend.
tests.test: in the FY2026 10-K (mid-November), owner earnings ≥ the ~$2.8B dividend, plus a disclosed uplift sales lift against control stores by the Q1 FY2027 print.
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Base to Bear (PW EV [[test3.pw_ev]], [[test3.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test3.verb]]**; the Outsider grade drops to Anti-Outsider for a dividend funded by debt.

return_math.epv: $26–35 per share (five-year owner earnings of $3.6B ÷ 9%; enterprise basis at the 15.5% median margin ≈$26). About two-thirds of the price pays for growth. The Bear ($69) sits well above EPV because it keeps ~5% growth and a 20× multiple; a no-growth Bear would be ≈$35.
return_math.base_rate: The Bull needs only ~5–6% nominal (~3% real) revenue growth, the FY2028 target; for companies above $25B, 31.8% reach 5% real growth over five years, so it is plausible. The constraint is margin, not sales.
return_math.year_ten: Still growing mid-single digits through licensed international stores and royalties; in the Bull the terminal multiple does much of the work.
